Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: pixel-art ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET for UMBRAL, first-person retro shooter. Reference image is the approved enemy design; preserve exact character identity, anatomy, material palette, weapons, face and gritty 1990s sprite style. Expand its poses into ONE NEW SHEET, portrait aspect 4:5, ideally 2048x2560 pixels, EXACTLY 4 columns and 5 rows = 20 equally sized square cells. Each row is one animation described below, each column its successive frame. Absolutely NO labels, text, grid lines, scenery or ground shadows. Background truly transparent. ONE creature per cell, never duplicate or spill into neighboring cell. All frames frontal player-facing view, fixed orthographic camera, fixed scale across entire sheet. Same ground baseline at 88% of each square cell, horizontal origin at center. Standing figure occupies 65% of cell height with margin for weapons and effects; dying figure naturally becomes much shorter on same baseline, do NOT enlarge the corpse. Leave 8% transparent padding around all cell edges. Crisp chunky hand-dithered pixel art, no smooth painting/antialias or photorealism. Full body and effects entirely inside each cell. Distinct readable keyframes with consistent equipment/anatomy. Fantasy creature gore is stylized pixel art. Do NOT include first-person arms, knife, execution or glory kill; only the enemy's own actions.

ROW 2 ATTACK: right claw reaches into burning chest; pulls out red molten flesh stone; throws it toward viewer with extended arm; recovers empty hand. ROW 3 HURT: torso snaps left from impact; head recoils; shoulders fall; regains stance. ROW 4 STAGGER: knees bent, chest exposed, head hangs, arms slack; four subtle swaying frames, amber furnace sputters, distinct vulnerable silhouette. ROW 5 DEATH: chest fire erupts; knees collapse; falls forward; low immobile ash-and-bone corpse with extinguished chest.
